items.prompt: Two pointers shine when each move?
choices: Permanently discards a region so total advances are O(n)
Randomly teleports both indices
Requires sorting after every step
Needs a segment tree
items.whyRight: Left and right only move forward (or inward) a linear number of times.
whyWrong: Random jumps lose the linear bound.

items.prompt: Pair-sum in a sorted array with two ends moving is?
choices: O(n) after the sort
O(n²) inevitably
O(n!)
items.whyRight: One pass of inward pointers once sorted.
whyWrong: Nested loops are the naive version.
Constant time cannot read n inputs.

items.prompt: Removing duplicates in-place from a sorted array uses slow/fast pointers to?
choices: Write the next unique value at the slow index
Delete via a new linked list only
Hash every index
Sort descending repeatedly
items.whyRight: Fast scans; slow marks the write frontier for uniques.
whyWrong: Extra lists use more space than needed.
Hashing works but is not the classic in-place sorted approach.

items.prompt: Opposite of a valid two-pointer move?
choices: Moving an index backward over a region you already discarded without a new invariant
Advancing the right end of a window
Moving left past a processed unique run
Closing ends when sum is too large
items.whyRight: Reopening discarded territory without a plan breaks O(n).

items.prompt: Container-with-most-water style problems move the pointer at the?
choices: Shorter line, hoping width loss is repaid by height
Taller line always
Middle always
Random end
items.whyRight: Height is limited by the shorter side; replace that side.
whyWrong: Moving the taller cannot increase the min height.
Middle probes are binary-search flavored, not this pattern.

items.prompt: When should you prefer hashing over two pointers for pair sums?
choices: Unsorted input where you want expected O(n) without sorting
Already sorted and O(1) extra space is required
You need the lexicographically smallest pair only via sort
Input is a linked list without values
items.whyRight: Hashing avoids the sort when order is absent and space is OK.
whyWrong: Sorted + tight space is two pointers’ home.
Lists need a different plan entirely.
